summary: Two red range lights that led vessels over the bar at Murray Harbour, PEI: a 1869 station, Penny family keepers, and a 2010 storm followed by a 2011 reset.

structures.note: Lowered by 3 m (10 ft) in 1902 so the rear light could be seen more easily.

staffing.note: Electrified 1963 (Lighthouse Friends) or 1966 (PEI Lighthouse Society); keepers stayed on as caretakers.

access.note: Front light reached on foot from Beach Point; tower closed. Rear light stands on private property.

events.note: Front light on a post, rear light on a barn gable; station established 1869.
After an inspection, a new lantern, lamps and reflectors were supplied.
Range towers built by Joseph Egan under an $850 contract, completed November 1878. The Lighthouse Directory gives 1879.
Front tower block encased in hemlock boards before the fall gales, as a temporary measure.
Front tower lowered 3 m (10 ft) so the back light could be more easily distinguished.
Front tower moved to the tip of the point (PEI Lighthouse Society only; not confirmed in the Marine reports read).
Lights electrified; keepers continued as caretakers at reduced salary (Lighthouse Friends). PEI Lighthouse Society gives 1966.
December 2010 storm surge swept the front tower off its foundation; Coast Guard retrieved it and left it on its side.
Front tower set on a new concrete foundation a short distance from the old one, 27 July 2011; reactivated.

corrections.why: The 1869 date marks the first post light. The present front tower is dated 1878 by Lighthouse Friends and the PEI Lighthouse Society (the Directory gives 1879).
The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights and the Lighthouse Friends history both give the front tower as 7.2 m (23.6 ft).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1869 was the first post and barn-gable light. The present towers are dated 1878 by Lighthouse Friends and the PEI Lighthouse Society and 1879 by the Lighthouse Directory. The story states both.
The record's 1869 first-lit date is the station's establishment (LF, Directory) before the towers were built in 1878.

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-27 against the cached Lighthouse Friends front and rear pages, the PEI Lighthouse Society front and back range pages, the Lighthouse Directory (ibiblio) entries and the Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights entries H0954 and H0954.1. OCR-matched by column position: the 1909-10 keepers' table (1911v45i13p21_0744, scan p. 255, printed p. 253). The page image was read: Murray Harbour Inner, Robert Penny, Nov. 11, 1897; Outer, Lemuel McLeod, Dec. 21, 1897. Both confirmed. The 1901-02 report (1903v37i8p21_0139) covers the fiscal year ended 30 June 1902; the November 1902 lowering is a plan in that report. Printed page and scan page for footnotes 7 and 9 agree in the corpus OCR index (no '?'). Disagreements stated in the text: the 1902 report expected a 20 ft (6.1 m) tower and the present tower is 7.2 m (23.6 ft); the keeper list starts in 1868, a year before the 1869 station start; electrification 1963 (LF) vs 1966 (PEI Society); last Penny 1963 (LF) vs 1966 (PEI Society); signatures 1,700 (LF) vs over 3,000 (PEI Society). Single-source: the 1908 move of the front tower (PEI Society only); the 1874 inspection and 1876 visit (LF only; the corpus starts in 1900). Not stated in the text: the Directory gives the rear light as about 1.5 km (almost a mile) from the front, the List gives 1,360.9 m; the Directory gives the front tower as 6 m (20 ft) with a 6.5 m focal plane, the List gives 7.2 m and 6.3 m; the List's figures are used. Robert Penny, Jr. (PEI Society, 1944-1966) is linked to Robert Curtis Penny (LF, 1944-1963) only by the shared 1944 start; the text says the two lists appear to name the same keeper. Source spellings kept: 'James Isaac Newton William', 'Malcom McFadyen'; LF spells the 1944 keeper 'Robert Curtis Penney' in its narrative. No USLHS roster exists for Canada; the roster is built from LF and the PEI Society, with Department lists as the check. The story has six chapters: the 1963 electrification moved to a new 'After the keepers' chapter. At about 1,300 words with annual reports, a keeper record and two histories, it fits the rich band, so all chapters with material are kept. No wreck or rescue tied to these lights was found in the sources read. Wikipedia and the CBC pages (the latter timed out) were not cited.
